\section{Discussion}
\label{sec:discussion}

\examplesys{} serves more requests from the cache than a recency-only cache on the synthetic trace (Table~\ref{tab:hits}).
The gain comes from requests that repeat in pairs.

\begin{table}[t]
\caption{Cache hit rate on the synthetic trace.}
\label{tab:hits}
\centering
\begin{tabular}{lr}
Cache & Hit rate \\
Recency only & 48.0\% \\
\examplesys{} & 59.25\% \\
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

\textbf{Limitations.} The trace is synthetic, so the gain on real traffic is not measured.
A trace of real traffic would settle it.

Prediction from recent pairs is a cheap way to cut misses when request patterns shift.
